title: Quiz — look up at the roof: what is the weather doing?
subtopic: 9 — The platform (Quiz B, before the dialogue)
learning_goal: Know that the departure night is dark and rainy, not foggy; know the pea-souper was a winter, coal-smoke thing.

narration.script: Twenty to nine, still under the roof. Look up — what is the weather doing tonight?
narration.after_script: Rain, then — Verne's words: 'The night was dark, and a fine, steady rain was falling.' Save the pea-souper for a winter chapter.

variants.clear: Twenty to nine, still under the roof. Look up — what is the weather doing tonight?

after_script_variants.clear: Rain, then. Verne's words: 'The night was dark, and a fine, steady rain was falling.' No fog tonight — we save the pea-souper for a winter chapter.

overlays.text: Look up at the roof — what is the weather doing tonight?
pea-souper — a thick yellow London fog

interaction.prompt: Twenty to nine, on the platform. Look up at the roof — what is the weather doing tonight?

options.feedback: The cliché — but London's great fogs were winter, coal-smoke things; the notorious one came in December 1873, the year after Fogg left.

options.text: A dark night and a fine, steady rain
options.feedback: Verne's own words. Rain on the station roof, then rain on the carriage window.
Not in October. Verne gives rain — and no fog either; save the pea-souper for a winter chapter.

production_notes: QUIZ B NOW PRECEDES THE DIALOGUE (D4): 15 → 16 quiz → 17 Passepartout → 18. The guide names no weather before the reveal (R5): question ≈ 8 s (script), pause until the choice or 20 s (pause_narration/timeout_s), option feedback, then narration.after_script states Verne's sentence. Upstream spoilers removed: 11 mackintosh feedback, 12 'wet stone'; nothing in 13–15 names the weather. Passepartout may say 'raining' freely in 17. Linear cut: the guide asks and states the answer (script + after_script), 15 s, no choice.
